SolarEdge — key metrics pack from the desk series file. Latest print in file: FY2026Q3 (period end 2026-09-30).

Through the quarter ended September 30, 2026 · weekly marks through the week ending November 8, 2026

The business

SolarEdge sells the electronics that sit between solar panels and the grid. A small optimizer on each panel feeds a central inverter, and monitoring software runs on top. It also sells home batteries and commercial three-phase systems. Almost all revenue is hardware sold to distributors and large installers, booked when it ships.

So revenue follows installer demand and how much stock the channel holds. Sales rose about fivefold from 2017 to 2022, then fell 70% in two years as distributors ran down inventory and European home solar slowed. Revenue recovered 31% in 2025. In Q3 2026 it was $326 million, 4% below a year earlier, and the company guided Q4 to $245–275 million.

The mix is moving. Batteries brought in $122 million in Q3, up 57%, and are now the largest product line, while optimizer and inverter sales fell by almost a third. Q3 gross margin of 33.2% includes a $36.0 million refund of tariffs paid earlier, which the Q4 guide leaves out. Free cash flow was positive for a fifth straight quarter.

Risks

  • Demand: residential solar in Europe and the U.S. depends on rates, subsidies and net-metering rules. Watch quarterly revenue and trailing free cash flow.
  • Pricing: Chinese inverter makers compete hard on price, especially outside the U.S.
  • Policy: U.S. manufacturing credits, tariffs and inverter import rules move gross margin and what can be sold.
  • Losses: still loss-making through September 2026, so the earnings multiple stays blank.

Close competitors

  • Enphase — microinverters on each panel, the main U.S. rival.
  • Tigo — panel-level optimizers that work with other brands' inverters.
  • SMA Solar — the German string-inverter maker.
  • Huawei and Sungrow — Chinese inverter makers that lead on volume and price.

Open gaps

  • Diluted EPS and shares, FY2015 Q1–Q2 (Jul–Dec 2014). Not printed: SolarEdge was private; no per-share figures were printed for those quarters (shares are pre-IPO counts).
  • Cash flow, FY2015 quarters. Not printed: quarterly cash flow before the IPO, so free cash flow starts in FY2016 Q1.
  • Growth rates, 2017 annual and FY2016T. Not comparable: 2016 was a June fiscal year plus a six-month transition, so there is no like-for-like prior year.
  • Q4 2016 (Oct–Dec) revenue and free cash flow. Calculated: cash flow is printed only for the six months to December 2016, so the quarter is the six months less Jul–Sep.
  • Trailing EPS for FY16 Q2–Q3, Q4 2016–Q3 2017, Q4 2020–Q3 2021 and Q3 2026; trailing free cash flow for Q4 2016–Q3 2017 and Q3 2026. Calculated: the sum of four printed quarters.
  • Q3 2026 figures. Data hold: read straight from the Q3 10-Q and earnings release; our shared data store has not captured the Q3 print yet.
  • Weekly multiples from the week ending Oct 4, 2026. Data hold: our shared weekly file still divides these weeks by June's trailing figures. We kept the same weekly prices and divided by the September trailing figures until the file catches up.
  • Employees before and after 2021. Basis change: SolarEdge printed full-time employees through 2020 and full- and part-time employees from 2021, so the two runs are separate series.
  • Revenue and net income per employee, FY2016T. Not comparable: the six-month transition period is not a full year.
  • Weekly PE and P/FCF before the week ending Aug 2, 2020. Data hold: daily prices in our store start July 27, 2020.
  • Forward earnings multiple. No sourced forward earnings estimate, so nothing is drawn.
  • Revenue by product line, units and battery megawatt-hours. History is on our SolarEdge product-lines page; this page shows the Q3 2026 prints on the key-metrics board.
